objectClass.primaryType: stepped radial fortress keep with an axial beam emitter
motionPotential: beam pulse along the vertical axis
objectClass.notes: 6-fold radial symmetry read from the visible arc of the plinth and pod ring; the rear hemisphere is inferred, not observed. The beam is volumeless light reconstructed as additive emissive geometry.

reasoning: Six macro tiers: base plinth, lower armour ring, mid-tier drum, crown collar, emitter basin, beam.
Four repetition systems drive most of the part count: 6 buttress feet, 6 lower pods, 6 drum fins, 8 collar plates.
Six material layers, two of them emissive at different hues, which the silhouette gates cannot see and the interior-difference gate must.
Occlusion risk is mid: radial symmetry lets the hidden hemisphere be inferred, but the drum behind the front pylon is unobserved.
Action readiness is real, not hypothetical: the game needs the beam to pulse and the structure to collapse tier by tier.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Choose simple/moderate/complex/ultra-complex from observed structure, not from a hardcoded domain.

details.description: An axial column of cyan light rising from the apex aperture, brightest at its base and falling to zero alpha at the top. No surface, no shading gradient across its width.
details.affects: emissive colour and intensity of the beam volume

details.description: A glowing torus ring lying flush in the floor of the crown basin, concentric with the aperture. Constant emission, reads as a light source spilling onto the basin walls.
details.affects: emissive colour, intensity and a matching point light

details.description: A crisp bright line along the top outer edge of every crown collar plate: a real chamfer catching grazing key light, not a painted highlight.
A cyan strip inset into the outward face of each collar plate, running with the plate's lean. Soft-edged glow, no relief: a recessed emissive strip, not an engraved groove.
details.affects: emissive inlay strip repeated once per collar plate

details.description: Two stacked amber horizontal bars on the front pylon head, the only warm hue on the upper structure. Lower value than the cyan, constant.
details.affects: emissive amber colour and intensity on stacked bar geometry

details.description: A dark recessed square on the pylon head carrying three short amber dashes and one pale square. Flat against the surface, no thickness.
details.affects: canvas-texture decal region on the dark gloss panel

details.description: The silver cap plates on the lower pods and buttresses hold a tight bright highlight along their crowns while the surrounding steel stays broad and soft: a localized low-roughness zone.
details.affects: roughness 0.18 over the cap plates against 0.55 on the body steel

details.description: Each lower pod carries a dark inset screen on its outward face, set below the surrounding plate: a real recess with its own dark gloss interior, not a dark patch.
details.affects: socket recess, depth 0.03 object-relative, interior uses glass-dark

details.description: A vertical cyan-lit channel recessed into the lateral face of each lower pod, with AO darkening at the channel mouth.
details.affects: negative relief channel, width 0.02 depth 0.02, emissive floor

details.description: The plinth's top rim is a wide chamfer, wider than any other bevel on the model, reading as a bright band all the way round the hexagon.
A round amber-lit boss at each plinth corner, one per hexagon vertex: a radially distributed instanced system with a hemispherical head, raised rather than countersunk.
details.affects: InstancedMesh, count 6, radial distribution, hemisphere head, emissive amber

details.description: The front entry ramp carries cyan strips across its treads, stepping down toward the viewer.
details.affects: emissive cyan strips repeated per tread

details.description: Loose grey gravel scattered on the plinth top in front of the structure, breaking the otherwise clean silhouette of the tier joint. Changes the silhouette, so geometry rather than a texture patch.
details.affects: instanced low-poly rock scatter, seeded, 18 pieces

details.description: Each tier meets the one below in a soft dark line rather than a hard groove: an AO seam, no measurable depth at this resolution.
details.affects: AO darkening along tier joints, no geometric relief

definitionOfDone: The rendered model matches the reference silhouette, primary proportions, visible component hierarchy, material response, and most recognizable local features for the selected fidelity tier.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

assumptions: Radial order is 6 for the plinth, foot, pod and fin rings, read from the plinth's visible corner angles rather than counted all the way round. Stated as a stylization.
The crown collar repeats 8 times, read from the visible arc; a top-down view would settle it.
The rear hemisphere is generated by radial repetition of the observed front, not observed.
The front ground-level feature is built as a recessed entry ramp; the reference cannot distinguish a ramp from a door or a vent at this resolution.
Bolt heads, the 3-dot status panel and seam widths are 1-3 px in a 156x199 reference, so they are reconstructed as plausible, not measured. The source sheet cannot provide a larger crop.
The beam is volumeless light in the reference; representing it as additive emissive geometry is a representation choice, not a measurement.

coordinateFrame.front: +Z, the face carrying the entry ramp and the pylon (camera-facing in the reference)
coordinateFrame.scaleReference: base plinth width = 2.0 object units; body height excluding the beam = 1.63, from the reference's measured 118 px body against its 145 px widest span (ratio 0.814)

silhouette.boundingShape: truncated hexagonal frustum, wider at the base, with a thin axial column rising from the apex
silhouette.symmetry: radial, order 6 (crown collar order 8); the front pylon and entry ramp are the only breaks in the repetition
dominantCurves: the stepped outer profile from plinth to crown, three inward jumps
the inward lean of the collar plates closing toward the aperture
negativeSpaces: the gaps between adjacent lower pods
the concave basin between the collar rim and the aperture

observations: Three stepped tiers, none sharing a radius with another.
Six-fold radial repetition on the plinth and lower ring; eight-fold on the crown collar.
Two emissive hues: cyan on the crown, slots and beam; amber on the plinth fascia and pylon.
Silver cap plates crown every pod and buttress and are the only low-roughness surfaces.
No wear, dirt or damage anywhere; the only broken-up surface is loose gravel on the plinth.

reviewHistory.summary: Blockout fails on structure, not polish. Three spec-side defects, each a wrong field contract rather than a wrong observation: (1) tier bodies were authored as 'cylinder' with geometryDescriptor.radialSegments, which the generator does not read, so every hexagonal tier came out as a smooth cylinder and, being an attachment primitive, was positioned from its attachment endpoint instead of its transform; (2) all four repetitionSystems used componentRef/type/radius/startAngleDegrees while the emitter reads level/parent/placement{mode,axis,radius,startAngleDeg}/instanceScale, so every ring fell through to unit boxes at the origin and no ring rendered; (3) child transform.position was authored in object space, but the generator applies it as the pivot Group's parent-local position, so each tier is offset by the accumulated height of its ancestors. The crown torus also needs rotation.x = -90deg to lie in the basin rather than stand beside it. For the record: silhouetteIoU scored 0.9199 on this render, a clean illustration of the documented trap -- the IoU is high because the wrong stack occupies roughly the right bounding cells.

What changed, with values: tier bodies became 'lathe' primitives with latheProfile.segments 6 (8 on the crown), which produces the true hexagonal footprint and carries each rim chamfer as a profile step; all child transform.position values were rewritten as parent-local; the four rings became explicitly authored member components with repetitionSystems declaring them via elementComponentIds, so the systems document the radial order instead of emitting a second cruder copy; the crown torus took rotation.x = -90deg and now lies in the basin. Proportions were then re-derived from a row-by-row measurement of the reference silhouette rather than the first pass's eyeballed 0.75 ratio: body height 1.63 against a 2.0 plinth (measured 0.814), tier heights 0.22 / 0.48 / 0.48 / 0.45, crown top radius closed from 0.42 to 0.28. Deterministic gates: tier-1 passed with map-stripped evidence (silhouetteIoU 0.9186, bilateral symmetry error 0.0065); the turntable gate passed at 0/90/180/270 with segmentationReliable true, which required teaching the lab to render on transparent -- against an opaque backdrop the gate reported every azimuth unsegmented and would have passed without ever measuring the subject; multi-angle found no degenerate view; the attachment anchor gate is clean. Interior difference against the reference is 0.098. What still does not match, all of it later-pass work: no emissive layer at all, the crown reads as a flat cap rather than a dome shoulder of leaning plates, the front pylon is buried behind the fin ring, and the plinth rim chamfer does not yet read as the bright band the reference shows.

Meso components join the macro tiers, so the rings, the front pylon and the crown ring are all in the tree with parent-child contracts: 49 components, hierarchy three deep at the pods, every child carrying parentSocket, localStart/localEnd, contactType, embed/overlap and gapTolerance. Two implementation contracts were corrected here, both found by reading the emitted factory rather than by guessing: (1) material.emissive is read as a hex STRING and material.emissiveIntensity as a number, so the descriptive emissive object this spec carried fell through to '#000000' and every emissive surface rendered dead -- the observation is preserved one field across as emissiveObservation and the beam now reads cyan; (2) the lab drove its PMREM room probe at full strength, which under ACES turned #2b333c metal at metalness 0.85 into mid grey, so the probe is now at 0.4 and does what it is for -- giving metal something to reflect -- while the battlefield's own three-light rig does the lighting. Gates: tier-1 passed with map-stripped evidence (silhouetteIoU 0.8883, bilateral symmetry error 0.056 -- higher than blockout's 0.0065 because the front pylon and the ramp are deliberate breaks in the radial symmetry); turntable passed at 0/90/180/270 with reliable segmentation; interior difference between the map-stripped and shaded renders is 0.057, which is the measure that the material layer is doing something inside the silhouette rather than only at its edge. Still absent, and correctly so at this pass: every emissive strip except the beam, the chamfer read on the plinth rim, the collar plate lean, and the recessed panels -- all of them micro-level, which the generator only emits from form-refinement onward.

featureReviews.notes: All five rings hold from every azimuth, and the micro level now carries the per-member detail: a cap plate on each pod, a lamp on each foot, a bar on each fascia band and each fin, an inlay on each collar plate.

The beam is axial, rooted at the aperture, and reads cyan; the basin is a real concave dish with the emitter torus lying flat in it. Residual: the beam is a hard-edged cylinder where the reference is a soft column that widens at its base and fades out at the top -- that is the additive/alpha work of the material pass, not geometry.

The plinth rim chamfer is real geometry -- a profile step in the 6-sided lathe, widened this iteration from a 0.045 to a 0.07 radial step -- and now reads as a continuous bright band around the hexagon under the key light, which is what the reference shows.

The ramp is present with four lit treads, and the plinth gravel is now 14 real faceted chips scattered deterministically (seed 20260903) across the front arc at radius 0.56-0.90, which is where the reference shows it. Its own detail entry had called for geometry rather than a texture patch; until this iteration it was a localFeature that could never render.

reviewHistory.summary: Form refinement, and the pass that found the defect the two before it were hiding. Three spec-side corrections, all root-caused in the emitted factory rather than guessed. (1) EVERY mesh in the model had been rendering as a unit primitive: scale_vector short-circuits on transform.scale when the key is present at all, and the authoring helper wrote an identity [1,1,1] onto every component, so dimensions were discarded model-wide. Removing the identity key restored the measured sizes and changed every proportion at once. This is precisely the class of defect silhouette IoU cannot see -- it scored 0.89-0.92 across all three passes while nothing in the model was the size it was specified to be. (2) The emissive strips existed only as component.localFeatures, which the generator reads for detail bookkeeping and never turns into geometry, so the two-hue emissive layout -- this model's strongest identity signal by its own analysis -- could not have rendered at any pass. Each strip is now a real micro component on its emissive material, with the localFeatures entry kept as the detail mapping: 6 foot lamps, 6 fascia bars, 6 pod slots, 6 pod bars, 6 fin bars, 8 collar inlays, 2 pylon bars, 4 ramp treads. (3) The authored root component emitted a real 2.0 x 1.63 x 2.0 box once dimensions were honoured, with the whole keep inside it; root is a pivot node, so its geometry is now a 1mm stub and its real extent lives on its collider. Then the pass gate itself caught a fourth: the important-feature average came in at 0.605 against a 0.650 threshold because the plinth gravel was still a localFeature, even though its own detail entry says it changes the silhouette and must be geometry. It is now 14 faceted chips scattered deterministically (seed 20260903) over the front arc at radius 0.56-0.90, and the plinth rim chamfer was widened from a 0.045 to a 0.07 radial profile step so it reads as the continuous bright band the reference shows. Component count 107. Gates: tier-1 passed with map-stripped evidence (silhouetteIoU 0.9103, bilateral symmetry error 0.0253); turntable passed at all four azimuths with reliable segmentation. Still not matching, and carried into the material pass: the render is lighter and lower-contrast than the reference's near-black steel, and the beam is a hard-edged cylinder where the reference is a soft column that widens at its base and fades to nothing at the top.

featureReviews.notes: Both hues are present and in the right places: amber on the plinth fascia, the foot lamps, the pod bars, the fin bars and the pylon stack; cyan on the pod slots, the collar inlays, the ramp treads, the emitter ring and the beam. Short of threshold because the reference's glow blooms into the plating around each strip and the render's does not -- the generator emits no bloom pass, so the strips read as bright paint rather than as light.
The beam is now a core plus a wider, dimmer halo shell, which approximates the reference's radial falloff without a blend mode. It still ends abruptly at the top where the reference fades to nothing.

The caps were enlarged and given to the buttress feet as well as the pods, and trim-silver moved from metalness 0.85 to 0.35 because at 0.85 the caps depended entirely on a probe that had to stay dim to keep the plating dark. They read lighter than the plating now, but not as the brightest thing on the model, which is what the reference shows.

reviewHistory.summary: Material pass, stopped at the bounded-correction limit with the tier-1 colour gate still failing. What the pass changed: steel albedo moved from the hand-sampled #2b333c to #1c2229 and metalness from 0.85 to 0.72, because the hand sample was read off a crop that still carried the reference's key light and sat about a stop light -- extract_pbr_evidence's palette for the same crop leads with #131518, and under ACES at 1.05 that difference was the whole gap between the render's mid grey and the reference's near-black plating. Every emissive surface was re-based: a self-lit strip's albedo is not its glow, so the strips moved to de-lit bases (#123240 cyan, #3a2a12 amber, consistent with the extracted palettes for those same crops) with the hue moved onto material.emissive and intensity raised to compensate. The beam gained a wider, dimmer halo shell as the code-only stand-in for an additive falloff the generator cannot emit. The silver caps were enlarged and extended to the buttress feet, and trim-silver dropped to metalness 0.35 because at 0.85 the caps depended entirely on a probe that has to stay dim for the plating to hold its value. BLOCKING RESULT, stated plainly: diagnose_render's per-part colour check fails at max delta-E 22.44 against a 20.0 threshold. Three bounded corrections moved it 68.13 -> 23.47 -> 22.45 -> 22.44, which is a plateau, not progress, so the loop stops here rather than churning. The residual is trim-silver: its measured albedo #8d9096 is further than 20 delta-E from any dominant colour cluster in the render, and it cannot get closer while the caps are a small share of a mostly-dark frame. That is the check's documented scope limitation -- it compares each component's colorMaterialRecipe against the render's OVERALL dominant clusters rather than a per-component crop -- and raising the probe to bring the caps up simply moved the outlier onto the dark steel instead (25.8). Resolving it properly needs per-component render crops, which the pipeline does not yet track; it is not resolvable by tuning this spec. Also unmet: emissive-layout scores 0.78 against 0.80 because the reference's glow blooms into the plating around each strip and this generator emits no bloom pass, so the strips read as bright paint rather than as light. Passes blockout, structural-pass and form-refinement are complete and credited; surface, lighting, interaction and optimization are not started.

Two-tone re-author from the high-res user reference: white armour dominant over dark structure, octagonal tiers, leaning white crown buttresses around a glowing pool, cyan louvres, corner antennas with lit tips, broad beam with halo. Root causes fixed this pass: (1) referencePbr maps wired as absolute filesystem paths 404'd in the browser and rendered black -- synthesized palette-grounded canvas maps now serve from /src; raw extractions kept as evidence with provenance; (2) flatShading killed lathe melt; (3) per-material envMapIntensity + scene env 0.15 fixed the earlier wash. Remaining gaps: no bloom pass so the pool glow reads as paint; rear hemisphere inferred; silhouette gate still fails on framing (beam doubles the auto-framed height vs the body-only reference crop).

Proportions pass 2 against the user's side-by-side: tiers squatted (body 1.63 to 1.38), plinth 2.6, all rings widened and tightened, pods converted to flush-capped panels, buttress lean calmed to 0.22, glowing cyan core dome added as the crown centerpiece with the beam rising from it, beam slimmed to 0.17/0.36 core/halo. Typecheck/lint/build green; turntable gate clean. Remaining: bloom for the dome/beam glow, rear hemisphere inferred.

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: This is an RTS structure drawn dozens of times per frame beside sixty units, so the budget is a build constraint, not a post-pass: every ring is one InstancedMesh and the six materials are shared across the tree.

lightingFromPhoto.evidence: Cap-plate highlights sit on the upper-front-left edge of every plate and the cast shadow falls back and right.
Shadowed faces stay legible and take a cool cast rather than going black.
The basin walls brighten toward the crown ring, which no external light in the reference could produce.

The emissive strips clip to near-white at their centres while the steel keeps its midtones, which is a filmic roll-off rather than a linear response. Matches the game renderer, so a model reads the same in the lab and in a match.
A soft ground shadow sits under the plinth rim and AO darkens every tier seam and recessed panel; without it the tiers read as stacked decals.

proceduralStrategy: Block out the four tier bodies as hexagonal prisms and check the stepped profile before any pod, fin or plate exists.
Add the four radial rings as InstancedMesh systems driven by repetitionSystems, never as hand-placed copies.
Chamfer the plinth rim and the collar plates as real geometry: the reference shows crisp bright edge lines that a normal map cannot produce.
Bind the six shared materials, then attach local overrides for the tier-seam AO, the cap gloss and the pylon decal.
Add the emissive layer last and verify it with interior_difference, not with silhouette IoU.
Keep every ring instanced and every material shared to stay inside 14k triangles and 12 draw calls.
animationAnchors: beam-column scales and pulses along Y from its base pivot; the aperture stays fixed
crown-ring brightens and scales with the beam charge (materialState + scale channels)
crown-collar-plate hinges outward about its own plate-hinge socket when the Core charges
pylon-head switches emissive state to signal production without any transform
root supports the whole-structure sink used when a Core is captured
destructionAnchors: fractureGroups run tier-0 (plinth) through tier-3 (collar and basin) so the keep collapses downward tier by tier rather than exploding outward
the tier seams (plinth-to-ring, ring-to-drum, drum-to-collar) are the declared break planes
lower-pod and crown-collar-plate carry detach:true and are the first fragments to leave
beam-column has fractureGroup none: the light stops, it does not shatter

risks.risk: If the true order is 8 rather than 6, pod spacing reads too sparse from above.
risks.mitigation: repetitionSystems.count is a single parameter per ring; changing it is a one-line spec edit, not a rebuild.

risks.risk: Silhouette IoU cannot see the emissive layout, which is the model's strongest identity signal; a Core with every light dead would pass a silhouette gate.
risks.mitigation: interior_difference.py plus the emissive-layout featureReviewTarget are the gates that actually read it.

risks.risk: The beam roughly doubles the model's bounding height, so an auto-framed review camera shrinks the keep itself to a third of the frame.
risks.mitigation: Review viewpoints frame on the body bounds and treat the beam as an overlay.

risks.risk: Panel decals and bolt layout cannot be scored against a 156 px reference.
risks.mitigation: Those details carry confidence <= 0.7 and are excluded from the critical feature set.
